profile.headline: Software Engineer at Kumiko Solutions | Custom software, app fixes, and workflow automation for small businesses
profile.summary:
I run Kumiko Solutions, a small software company in St. Louis. Most of my work falls into three buckets:

+ Building new software: websites, internal tools, and iOS and Mac apps
+ Fixing what's already there: unfinished apps, slow or broken sites, and AI-built code that got most of the way
+ Automating repetitive work: file handling, data entry, reports, and the spreadsheet everything runs on

I've also done AI training work on coding models, reviewing and correcting their software engineering output, so I know where AI-written code tends to go wrong. My own app, Rebacked, is on the Mac App Store.

Fixed price for a defined result, and you own the code and accounts when we're done.

projects.title: Kumiko Experiments
projects.description:
Three browser games, each one HTML file. No engine, no image or audio files. Everything is drawn in code.

- Hi-Lo Trainer: learn card counting in short drills
- Kitchen Sink: pressure-wash the grime off a pan, a rack, a dish and the sink
- Flight Recorder: take apart a flight recorder on a repair bench, one screw at a time. Best on a phone

Each one has its own animated entry page, and they all still work with reduced motion on.

projects.title: App Archaeology: a read-only storage inspector for macOS
projects.description:
A Mac utility I built and shipped on the Mac App Store under Kumiko Solutions.

It shows where each installed app keeps its data (caches, containers, preferences, logs, launch items), how much space each app really uses, and what deleted apps left behind. It only reads. It never deletes a file and makes no network connection.

The hard part was the macOS sandbox. Some folders are always off limits, and macOS asks before an app can read another app's data. Scan Coverage shows which folders were checked and which ones macOS kept private, so the totals never claim more than they know.

SwiftUI, sandboxed, macOS 14 and later.
